name: jpy-notebook
description: One pane holding one or more Jupyter notebooks as TABS: every cell rendered natively — Markdown, syntax-lit source, and real outputs (streams with ANSI colour, pandas DataFrames as tables, PNG/JPEG/SVG figures, JSON trees, IPython tracebacks) — plus per-cell Run / Run-all / Interrupt / Restart against a live kernel. Reach for it whenever the user names a .ipynb, asks what a notebook produced, asks to run or re-run a cell or a notebook, or asks about an error in one. SERVICE-BACKED, and the only service in wc-jupyter: it reads the .ipynb as JSON (nbformat v4 — no Python needed for the read half) and speaks the Jupyter Server REST + WebSocket kernel protocol for the run half, using Node's global fetch and WebSocket with zero dependencies. EDIT AND SAVE: code cells are editable in the pane, a run carries the edited buffer (so 'run what I am looking at' needs no save first), and Save writes back through the Jupyter contents API (PUT /api/contents) rather than by writing the file - so a JupyterLab session with the same notebook open sees the change the way it expects. Two consequences worth knowing before you promise a save: saving REQUIRES a connected server, and the notebook must live under that server's root_dir - one outside it reports saveable:false with a hint and the Save button is disabled, because the contents API cannot address it. Outputs are never written back; only cell source is. The service keeps the ORIGINALLY PARSED notebook and mutates just cells[i].source, so cell metadata, attachments, raw cells, notebook metadata and nbformat_minor all survive a save untouched (verified by round-trip test; nbformat does canonicalise key ORDER on write, which is its serialiser, not data loss). Jupyter does no optimistic concurrency here, so the service compares last_modified itself and REFUSES a save when the file changed on disk since it was opened, reporting state 'stale' rather than clobbering someone else's edit. Markdown and raw cells are rendered but NOT yet editable. Being host code, its first run waits on a one-time TERMINAL approval — tell the user to run `claude-web-chat trust jpy-notebook`; the pane can only name the command, never grant it. TABS ARE RUNTIME-MUTABLE. `notebooks` (optional) seeds the tabs on mount; the pane can also Browse, Open, Create and Close notebooks via the ops 'browse' {dir?}, 'open' {path}, 'new' {dir?,name?} and 'close' {id}. THE BOUNDARY on anything the pane names is the `open_root` param - default the PROJECT ROOT, settable to an absolute path, or false to disable runtime opening. Every pane-supplied path goes through ctx.fence against it before reaching fs or the contents API; the contents API's own check is purely lexical and does not realpath, so it is NOT a substitute for the fence. 'browse' and 'open' are replay-safe; 'new' CREATES A FILE and 'close' removes a tab, so both are refused below the service start-time floor. A new notebook is created through the contents API (never through fs) seeded with one empty code cell. The live tab set is persisted beside the journal so runtime-opened tabs survive the service being stopped when its pane leaves the active node. Refusals ride jpy_nb.notice {seq, op, reason} - reasons 'outside-boundary', 'outside-server-root', 'not-a-notebook', 'tab-cap', 'no-server', 'exists', 'dirty-unsaveable', 'open-disabled'. Directory listings ride the transient key jpy_browse. The KERNEL CONNECTION IS DELIBERATELY NOT A PARAM — params are part of the trust fingerprint, so a URL or token there would re-prompt the terminal on every change; the user types the server URL and token into the pane instead, and the token field is type=password so it never lands in form_state or the event log. Start a server with `jupyter server --no-browser` (or use a running JupyterLab) and paste its URL + token. Reads the control key `jpy_ctl { seq, op }` — ops 'connect' {index}, 'discover', 'set-tab' {id}, 'edit' {cell,source}, 'run' {cell, source?}, 'run-all', 'save' {id?}, 'revert' {id?}, 'insert' {cell,where:'after'|'before',type}, 'delete' {cell}, 'move' {cell,to}, 'set-type' {cell,type}, 'interrupt', 'restart', 'reload'. STRUCTURAL OPS mutate only the in-memory projection; the file changes on the next save, which rebuilds the notebook's cell list from that projection BY ID — so an insert or a delete can never write one cell's text into its neighbour, and an untouched cell round-trips as the exact object read from the file. A cell inserted into an nbformat 4.5 notebook is minted a unique id ('u'+8 hex); one inserted into a 4.0-4.4 notebook gets NO id and the file stays at its own version, because adding ids is a format change those readers reject. Changing a cell's type rebuilds it for the target type (code gains execution_count+outputs, markdown/raw must carry neither) and is REFUSED for markdown->code when the cell has attachments, rather than silently dropping embedded images. Deleting a cell tombstones its jpy_out_<id> key. `seq` on every control write must be STRICTLY GREATER than the last applied — two writes in the same millisecond collide and the second is dropped. Only 'set-tab', 'reload' and 'discover' may replay after a respawn; 'save', 'edit' and every run op are refused below the service's start time, so navigating the graph can never resurrect a write. It is a CONTROL key, not a signal: the user running cells never wakes Claude. You may write it yourself to steer a live pane, but set_store needs its patch wrapper — `set_store({patch:{jpy_ctl:{seq:Date.now(), op:'run-all'}}})`; the unwrapped form is a silent no-op that still returns ok. A cell is COMPLETE when iopub reports status execution_state 'idle' for its msg_id, NOT when execute_reply arrives — measured: the reply lands first, so completing on it truncates trailing output. THERE IS NO SAVE OR REVERT BUTTON: the notebook AUTOSAVES (~1.2s after typing stops, 15s ceiling, immediately on a structural change, in parallel with a run, flushed on tab switch and shutdown) and a status chip reports whether that is working - `saved <time>`, `N unsaved`, or a clickable warning for a failure, a disk conflict, or an unsaveable notebook. UNDO HAS TWO SCOPES. Every cell carries per-cell UNDO and REDO buttons that rewind THAT cell only, via the `cell-undo` op {cell, dir, source?, rev?} - dir -1 undoes, dir 1 redoes. `jpy_hist.cells` and `jpy_hist.cells_redo` are sparse maps saying which cells have anything in each direction, so both buttons know whether they are live without re-reading the journal. UNDO walks the on-disk journal; REDO is an in-memory stack of the values undone away from, because every cell-undo seals a new version and so a forward walk would re-encounter the walk's own history and never exhaust - which means redo does NOT survive a service respawn while undo does - it seals the live buffer first, then walks the journal for the nearest version where that cell's source differs, so repeated taps walk back rather than toggling and a duplicated click is a no-op. jpy_hist.cells is a sparse {cellId: rev} map saying which cells have a prior value, so the button knows whether it is live without re-reading the journal. The toolbar Undo/Redo (ops `undo`/`redo`/`goto-rev`) walk a DOCUMENT history kept on host disk under <webChatDir>/jpy-history/, which survives the pane being destroyed, the service stopping and the daemon restarting. Undo transports as 'be at revision N', never as a delta, so a duplicated click cannot over-rewind. Undo does NOT un-run a cell or restore a previous run's outputs. Markdown and raw cells ARE editable: an Edit/Done toggle, double-click the preview to edit, Escape or Cmd+Enter to render, and an EMPTY markdown cell always shows its editor rather than an invisible empty preview (which is what makes a just-inserted one usable). MOUNT IT WITH `params.routing:'none'`. Running a cell writes `jpy_ctl`, and an undeclared browser store write made near a click coalesces into the queue rail as generic pane activity - so without the opt-out every Run the user makes shows up as something they never asked to send. Declared signals are NOT affected by the opt-out (lib/channel/policy.js classify() consults routing only on the no-declared-key branch), so `jpy_ask` still queues. Note `routing` goes INSIDE params while `signals` goes TOP-LEVEL on use_component; the wrong one is dropped with no error. The pane declares ONE signal, `jpy_ask` {seq, notebook, cell, kind, note}, and there are three deliberate affordances per cell: Run (control key only - Claude is never told), Run + tell Claude, and Ask Claude. The latter two open an inline note box and write `jpy_ask` with the user's own `note` (null when they sent it empty); `kind` is 'run-and-report', 'traceback' or 'cell'. Read the note - it is the user saying what they actually want looked at. Read `jpy_nb` for the tab list and per-cell STRUCTURE (id, type, exec_count, len, `head` = first non-blank line, truncated) — it deliberately carries NO source. Cell source is on `jpy_src_<cellId>` {source, truncated}, published only for the ACTIVE tab and only when the FILE state changes (load, reload, revert, tab switch, a save that altered content) — never while the user types, because the pane owns the live buffer and every store write is copied into every committed graph node. Read `jpy_out_<cellId>` for that cell's outputs and state — outputs are capped per cell and the cap is reported rather than silently applied. `application/javascript` outputs and ipywidgets are rendered as inert source with a badge, never executed.

notebooks.title: Notebooks to open on mount
notebooks.description: ABSOLUTE paths to .ipynb files to open as tabs on mount, in order. OPTIONAL: the pane can open more at runtime within `open_root`. These specific paths are named on the terminal approval line, so they may sit OUTSIDE open_root and are still read — the existing readable-and-runnable-but-not-saveable case applies when they are also outside the Jupyter server root. A relative path is refused with reason "not-absolute"; a missing or unparseable file becomes a tab that explains itself rather than a silent gap.

active.title: Tab to open first
active.description: Which notebook to show on mount — an absolute path from `notebooks`, or its bare filename. Omit to open the first. An unmatched value falls back to the first tab and says so on jpy_conn.

open_root.title: Boundary for notebooks the pane may open
open_root.description: THE CONSENT BOUNDARY for anything the PANE names at runtime — Open, New and Browse. Every pane-supplied path is put through the daemon's fence against this directory before it reaches the filesystem or the Jupyter contents API, and the fence refuses a lexical ../.. AND a symlink resolving out of the tree. Omit it and the boundary is the PROJECT ROOT, which is already part of the trust key. Set an absolute path to widen or narrow it — it prints literally on the approval line, which is the strongest disclosure available. Set it to false to disable runtime opening entirely, which is the pre-0.2 behaviour. It is deliberately NOT the connected Jupyter server's root_dir: that is chosen by the pane's server picker and appears nowhere in the trust fingerprint, so one `jupyter lab ~` would silently widen the boundary to your home directory while the approval still read notebooks=[...].
